solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Remark about right part of train for best views

definitions.text: part of train for best views

parts.note: a remark is a comment, an observation
CA, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: Someone recommending the spot on a train with the finest scenery.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway carriage with large windows built for passengers to enjoy scenery is the descriptive name for this kind of carriage.

clue.text: Barely working — extremely lazy, right?

parts.note: a machine that is working is switched on

indicators.note: extremely means take the two extreme letters of the word lazy

parts.note: just means right or fair

explanation.surface: An idler is hardly doing any work, and someone checks that this is true.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean by the narrowest of margins, hardly at all.

clue.text: Rich relative with gold ring (American)

parts.note: a son is a family relative
OR is gold in heraldry
the letter O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A wealthy family member showing off a gold ring from America.
explanation.definitionFit: A rich voice or sound is deep and full, which is exactly what sonorous describes.

clue.text: Calls Kosovo regularly?

definitions.meaning: to call someone on the phone is to give them a ring
every second letter of the word Kosovo is an O, a ring shape, so it regularly has these round letters

explanation.surface: Someone phoning the Balkan state Kosovo on a regular basis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' looks like an alternate-letter signal, and it is: the even letters of KOSOVO are O, O, O, each a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: To phone someone is to give them a buzz; the plural verb matches the plural noun for O shapes.

clue.text: "Unhesitatingly a bum crack!" "Pardon?"

indicators.note: um is a hesitation sound, so without hesitating the word bum loses those two letters

parts.note: to crack a puzzle is to solve it

explanation.surface: A cheeky exclamation about a bottom, met with a puzzled request to repeat it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pardon?' looks like a request to hear it again, but it is a verb meaning forgive.
explanation.definitionFit: To forgive someone formally, especially of sin, is to absolve them.

clue.text: Spaced out female superhero

parts.note: split the word female with a space and it reads FE MALE: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron, and a male is a man

explanation.surface: A dazed or drugged-up heroine from the comics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spaced out' seems to mean dazed; it says to put a space in the word female.
explanation.definitionFit: Tony Stark's armoured alter ego is a Marvel comics hero, so this is an example of the category.

clue.text: TV or radio programmes with young actors on board

parts.note: something young is new

indicators.note: to be on board is to be in the ship, so the actors are put inside the steamship letters

parts.note: SS, a steamship, is the thing you are on board
the actors in a play are its cast

explanation.surface: Broadcasts that bring youthful performers into the line-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Bulletins of news broadcast on television or radio are programmes of this kind.

clue.text: See 1
It's charged when ordering a tonic

indicators.note: ordering the letters of a tonic means arranging them anew

explanation.surface: A bar bill: you pay a fee when you order a tonic water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charged' looks like paying money; it means carrying electric charge.
explanation.definitionFit: In chemistry a positively charged ion is the particle meant, so it is literally something charged.

clue.text: What appears in ill-advised reworking of material

indicators.note: the word for what shows up inside the word for ill-advised

parts.note: a rash decision is ill-advised
eh? is a way of saying what?

explanation.surface: Something that shows up in a poorly judged rewrite of old content.
explanation.definitionFit: A rewrite that presents old material again with little change is a rehash, a recycling of content.

clue.text: Brand new bedclothes?

parts.note: a brand of goods is a product line

explanation.surface: Asking whether some freshly bought sheets are brand new.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheets and pillowcases are collectively called household linen, hence the question mark for this loose example.

clue.text: Sample book about first-timer in race

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the sample book goes around the word for first

parts.note: a swatch is a book of fabric samples
to be top is to come first

explanation.surface: Someone testing a book about a novice runner in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first-timer' reads as a novice; split it, 'first' is TOP and 'timer in race' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Officials time runners with a handheld device started and stopped by hand, which is a timer used in races.

clue.text: Christian heraldic device appearing in famous song burden

parts.note: Jerusalem is the famous English hymn set to Blake's words, 'And did those feet'
a cross to bear is a burden

explanation.surface: A religious emblem on a coat of arms appears in a well-known song's refrain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'burden' also means a song's refrain, which suits the surface; here it is a load to carry. Jerusalem is a hymn sung at English national occasions.
explanation.definitionFit: A heraldic cross with smaller crosses in its angles, associated with the Holy Land, is this named emblem.

clue.text: See 11
Modest hotel, having gone for road trip

indicators.note: the hotel letter has gone and the road letters take its place

parts.note: a modest person is humble
H is hotel in the phonetic alphabet
ST is short for street, a road

explanation.surface: A cheap hotel abandoned in favour of a road trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'road trip' looks like one phrase; 'road' is wordplay and 'trip' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To trip is to lose one's footing, the same as a stumble.

clue.text: Sleeping partner fled, after hiding under covers

indicators.note: the word for under goes around the shuffled letters

parts.note: below means under

indicators.note: a hiding is a beating, so after one the letters of fled are knocked about

explanation.surface: A lover who ran off after hiding beneath the bedclothes.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'hiding' is a beating, so the letters are knocked about; they come out as DFEL. 'under covers' suggests a bed but 'under' is the outer word.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who shares your bed is literally a sleeping partner; the phrase also hints at a business sense.

clue.text: Architect or poet from Northwood

parts.note: ash is a type of wood

explanation.surface: A designer or writer who comes from Northwood, a London suburb.
explanation.walkthrough: Northwood is a suburb of north-west London; split into North and wood it spells the surname.
explanation.definitionFit: John Nash designed Regency London; Ogden Nash wrote comic verse, so the surname fits both.

clue.text: Welshman caught intercepting letter for ex-wife?

indicators.note: the Welshman and the caught letter cut into the spelt-out letter

parts.note: dee is the spelt name of the letter D
Ivor is a typically Welsh man's name
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A Welshman nabbed while snatching a letter meant for his former wife.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman whose marriage has been legally ended is a former spouse; the question mark notes it need not be a wife.

clue.text: Anticipates rider possessing bad temper

indicators.note: the rider letters hold the shuffled temper inside them

parts.note: a PS (postscript) is a rider, an addition to a document

indicators.note: bad signals the letters of temper are put in disorder

explanation.surface: A horseman with a foul mood expects trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' makes REEMPT. 'rider' looks like a horseman, but it is an addendum to a document, as a postscript is.
explanation.definitionFit: To act first to forestall something expected is to anticipate it, a close synonym.

clue.text: Book of poems having partly influenced Dante

indicators.note: partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A collection of verse that had some influence on Dante.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft put 'having' in the definition; it is a link word, since 'Book of poems having' cannot stand in for a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The Icelandic collections of Norse mythological verse are known by this name, so it is a book of poems.

clue.text: Coffee originally cultivated in part of SW Asia

indicators.note: the first letter goes inside the region's name

parts.note: Arabia is the peninsula in south-west Asia

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter of cultivated

explanation.surface: Coffee first grown in the Middle East.
explanation.definitionFit: The bean variety from the plant Coffea arabica is the most widely grown kind of coffee.

clue.text: Sack race his undoing?

indicators.note: undoing the letters of race his scrambles them into a new order

explanation.surface: Asking whether a sack race was a competitor's downfall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sack race' looks like one phrase; 'Sack' is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismiss someone from the armed forces in disgrace is to cashier them, so to sack them.

clue.text: Gulf state heard discharge complaint

indicators.note: heard tells us the name of the state is said aloud

parts.note: Qatar is a state on the Persian Gulf

explanation.surface: A Gulf nation hears a grievance about dismissal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discharge complaint' looks like a protest at being fired; it is an ailment with discharge.
explanation.definitionFit: This illness is an excess of mucus in the nose or throat, a complaint involving discharge.

clue.text: Return missing top that's way- out

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter, which is dropped

parts.note: to regress is to return to an earlier state

explanation.surface: A comeback without its best part is far-out, man.
explanation.definitionFit: An exit is the way out of a building, and the formal word for an exit is this one.

clue.text: That hurts, when described by rising journalist as a contemptible person

indicators.note: to be described by is to have a line drawn round you, so the reversed journalist goes around the cry of pain
in a down clue, rising means the letters read upwards

parts.note: ED is short for editor, a journalist
ouch is what you say when something hurts

explanation.surface: A columnist calls someone a creep, and that stings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' makes DE, since a down entry reads upwards when reversed; 'described' is used in the geometric sense of drawing a boundary round something.
explanation.definitionFit: In American slang the word is an insult for an obnoxious, despicable man.

clue.text: Blog about rocket he and I ordered with a vegetable

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so the letters of blog are rearranged
ordered says the letters of rocket he, I and a are put into a new sequence

explanation.surface: An online diary on a rocket salad prepared with another vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns BLOG into GLOB; 'ordered' rearranges ROCKETHEIA into EARTICHOKE.
explanation.definitionFit: This thistle-like plant has an edible flower head, eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: See 23
Friend on piano is a Blockhead

parts.note: a chum is a friend
P is the music abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A pal at the keyboard is an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are insults for a foolish, dim person.

clue.text: Spreadsheet software's input output runs hotel

parts.note: Excel is Microsoft's spreadsheet program, here with its possessive s
I is short for input
O is short for output
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A spreadsheet program's data flow runs a hotel's systems.
explanation.definitionFit: Many grand hotels carry this Latin name meaning higher, so it is a common hotel name.

clue.text: Remove cover from a French contraceptive

parts.note: un is French for a
a cap is a contraceptive diaphragm

explanation.surface: Taking the wrapper off a contraceptive bought in France.
explanation.definitionFit: To take the lid or top off something is to remove its covering.

clue.text: With new arrangement, a step-nephew has to play it by ear?

indicators.note: a new arrangement of the letters of a step-nephew has means they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A musical step-nephew, given a new arrangement, has to improvise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement' and 'by ear' both suggest music, steering away from the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: To improvise without planning, waiting on events, is the idiom; the question mark flags the musical phrase used loosely.
